scenes.heading: Choosing & Migrating Between Warehouses
scenes.narration: Picking a warehouse and moving to it are strategic decisions that hinge on your cloud, workloads, and team skills.

scenes.heading: How to choose
bullets: Match the warehouse to your primary cloud to avoid egress costs.
Weigh pricing models against your workload's shape and predictability.
Consider ecosystem fit: BI tools, connectors, and existing skills.
Value features you truly need, like sharing, over feature checklists.
scenes.narration: The strongest signal is usually your existing cloud, since staying native avoids data egress fees and integration friction. Next, match the pricing model to whether your usage is spiky or steady. Finally, weigh ecosystem fit and the specific features your teams will actually use rather than chasing long feature lists.

scenes.heading: The three major platforms

right.title: BigQuery & Redshift
points: Deeply native to GCP and AWS

scenes.narration: Snowflake is cloud-agnostic with elegant compute separation and best-in-class sharing. BigQuery is serverless and native to Google Cloud, billing by bytes scanned or reserved slots. Redshift is cluster-based and tightly integrated with AWS, making it natural for teams already invested there.

scenes.heading: A safe migration path
scenes.narration: A sound migration begins with an inventory of schemas, queries, and dependencies to size the effort. You then convert the schema and SQL dialect, backfill the historical data, and keep it in sync with incremental loads. Only after validating results in parallel do you cut traffic over and retire the old system.

scenes.text: Choose the warehouse that fits your cloud and workload, then migrate incrementally with parallel validation before cutover.
scenes.narration: Let your cloud and workload guide the choice, and de-risk the move by running old and new in parallel until you trust the new system.
